questionTextEn: The President of India is elected by:
optionBEn: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
optionCEn: All members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures
optionDEn: Elected members of Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies only
explanationEn: The Electoral College for the President consists of elected (not nominated) members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (Article 54). Nominated members and members of State Legislative Councils do not participate.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding the President's ordinance-making power is/are correct?
explanationEn: Under Article 123, the President can promulgate ordinances when either House is not in session. The ordinance must be laid before Parliament and ceases to operate 6 weeks after reassembly if not approved. All three statements are correct.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The 'Pocket Veto' of the President refers to:
optionAEn: Returning a Bill to Parliament for reconsideration
optionBEn: Withholding assent to a Bill indefinitely without any time limit
optionCEn: Seeking the opinion of the Supreme Court on a Bill
optionDEn: Giving assent to a Bill with conditions attached
explanationEn: Unlike the American President, the Indian President has no constitutional time limit to act on a Bill. By indefinitely withholding assent without returning it, the President exercises a 'Pocket Veto' (e.g., Indian Post Office Amendment Bill, 1986 by President Zail Singh).
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which article empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, and remissions of punishment?
explanationEn: Article 72 grants the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence under Union law, including court martial cases and death sentences.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Financial Emergency under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution:
optionAEn: Has been proclaimed twice in India's history
optionBEn: Requires approval of Rajya Sabha within two months
optionCEn: Has never been proclaimed in India
optionDEn: Can only be proclaimed during war
explanationEn: Financial Emergency (Article 360), which can be proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened, has never been invoked since the Constitution came into force in 1950.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: During President's Rule under Article 356, which of the following is/are true?
explanationEn: Under Article 356, the President can assume all executive functions, dissolve or suspend the State Legislature (which then cannot sit), and Parliament assumes state legislative powers. The Governor acts on behalf of the President.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The President can nominate how many members to the Rajya Sabha?
explanationEn: Under Article 80(1)(a), the President can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha who have distinguished themselves in literature, science, art, and social service.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Indian Constitution borrows the concept of Directive Principles of State Policy from the Constitution of:
explanationEn: The DPSPs in Part IV of the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Irish Constitution, which in turn was influenced by the Spanish Constitution.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following is NOT a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
optionBEn: Division of powers between Centre and States
explanationEn: Single Citizenship is a unitary feature. In a true federation like the USA, citizens have dual citizenship (national + state). India has only one (Indian) citizenship.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The provision of 'Single Integrated Judiciary' in India means:
optionAEn: There is only one court in India
optionBEn: The Supreme Court is the only appellate court
optionCEn: The judiciary forms a single hierarchy with the Supreme Court at the apex
optionDEn: High Courts have no independent power
explanationEn: Unlike the USA which has separate federal and state court systems, India has a single integrated judicial hierarchy – Supreme Court → High Courts → Subordinate Courts – where all levels enforce both central and state laws.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which amendment added the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
explanationEn: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 (during Indira Gandhi's government) added the words 'Socialist,' 'Secular,' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following features make the Indian Constitution rigid?
explanationEn: The rigidity comes from requiring special majority (2/3rds present and voting + absolute majority), plus ratification by half the states for some amendments, and mandatory Presidential assent for all amendments.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The concept of 'Fundamental Duties' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
explanationEn: Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment based on the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee recommendation and inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Indian Constitution provides for a 'Parliamentary form of government' which means:
explanationEn: In a Parliamentary system, the executive (Council of Ministers) is responsible to the Legislature (Lok Sabha). The President is the nominal head while the Prime Minister is the real executive. Statement 2 is incorrect — the President is the nominal head.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on:
explanationEn: The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28 January 1950 (two days after the Constitution came into force), replacing the Federal Court of India established under the Government of India Act, 1935.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Under which article can the Supreme Court issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
explanationEn: Article 32 empowers the SC to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul of the Constitution.' Article 226 is for High Courts.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The 'Collegium System' for the appointment of Supreme Court judges was established through:
explanationEn: The Collegium System evolved through the Second Judges Case (1993) and Third Judges Case (1998), where the SC interpreted Article 124 to establish that the CJI along with 4 senior-most judges form the collegium for appointments.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Special Leave Petition (SLP) can be filed in the Supreme Court under:
explanationEn: Article 136 grants the SC discretionary power to grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, order, or sentence of any court or tribunal in India. This is a vast power making the SC the ultimate appellate authority.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The retirement age of a Supreme Court judge is:
explanationEn: Supreme Court judges retire at 65 years of age (Article 124). High Court judges retire at 62 years. This distinction is important for competitive exams.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Supreme Court's Advisory Jurisdiction is provided under:
explanationEn: Under Article 143, the President can refer any question of law or fact of public importance to the SC for its opinion. The SC may report its opinion. This is advisory and not binding on the President.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: A Supreme Court judge can be removed from office by:
optionCEn: An address by both Houses of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity
optionDEn: A resolution of the Lok Sabha alone
explanationEn: Under Article 124(4), a SC judge can be removed only by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. This is called 'impeachment.'
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution vests the superintendence and control of elections in:
explanationEn: Article 324 vests the Election Commission with the power of superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and offices of President and Vice-President.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as:
optionCEn: A Judge of the Supreme Court
explanationEn: The CEC enjoys the same security of tenure as a Supreme Court judge and can only be removed through impeachment — by an address of both Houses of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: NOTA (None of the Above) option in Indian elections was introduced following the Supreme Court judgment in:
explanationEn: In the PUCL v. Union of India case (2013), the Supreme Court directed the Election Commission to provide a NOTA option in EVMs, giving voters the right to reject all candidates.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following elections are NOT conducted by the Election Commission of India?
optionAEn: Elections to the State Legislative Assembly
explanationEn: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by State Election Commissions (Article 243-K and 243-ZA), not the Election Commission of India.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Election Commission became a multi-member body in its present form in:
explanationEn: While it was briefly made multi-member in 1989 (reverted in 1990), the current three-member structure (CEC + 2 ECs) was established in 1993 through the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Conditions of Service) Act amendment.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were used for the first time on a universal basis in all constituencies in:
explanationEn: While EVMs were introduced in selected constituencies from 1998 onwards (first in Kerala bye-elections in 1982 on a trial basis), they were used universally across all constituencies for the first time in the 2004 General Elections.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Model Code of Conduct comes into effect:
optionAEn: From the date the election schedule is announced
optionDEn: One month before the election date
explanationEn: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force immediately upon the announcement of the election schedule by the Election Commission and remains in force until the completion of the election process.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains:
optionBEn: Three lists dividing legislative subjects between Centre and States
optionCEn: The forms of oaths or affirmations
explanationEn: The Seventh Schedule contains three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List, which distribute legislative subjects between the Parliament and State Legislatures.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: In case of conflict between a Central law and a State law on a subject in the Concurrent List:
optionCEn: The President decides which law prevails
explanationEn: Under Article 254, if there is a conflict between Central and State legislation on a Concurrent List subject, the Central law prevails and the State law becomes void to the extent of repugnancy. However, if the State law has received Presidential assent, it may prevail in that State.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under:
explanationEn: Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission every five years (or earlier) to recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and States.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Residuary powers of legislation belong to:
explanationEn: Under Article 248, the Parliament has exclusive power to make any law on a matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or the State List. Entry 97 of the Union List further reinforces this residuary power with the Union.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Sarkaria Commission was set up to examine:
explanationEn: The Sarkaria Commission, established in 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria, examined and recommended changes in Centre-State relations. It submitted its report in 1988 with 247 recommendations including restraint on Article 356, strengthening Inter-State Council, etc.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Inter-State Council is constituted under which Article?
explanationEn: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council to investigate and advise on inter-state disputes and to make recommendations for better coordination of policy and action. It was established in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: GST (Goods and Services Tax) was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
explanationEn: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 introduced GST in India, establishing the GST Council (Article 279A) to recommend rates, exemptions and other matters related to GST. It subsumed multiple Central and State indirect taxes.
subject: Polity
